# UX Conventions & Interaction Checklist: Accounts and invitations

**Purpose**: Validate that the interaction requirements — including the four cross-cutting conventions this entry implements first — are complete, quantified and consistent with the entry that states them
**Created**: 2026-08-30
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.
**Coverage pass, 2026-08-31**: every item was re-read against `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `research.md`, `data-model.md`, `contracts/`, entry R1's and R2's artifacts, `docs/product/specifications.md` and `AGENTS.md`. Items marked **Covered** were already answered by one of those, and each names where — so a criterion satisfied by a design artifact rather than by `spec.md` is visible as such. Items marked **Resolved** were answered by amending `spec.md` in the same pass, and name the requirement that now carries them.

**Scope note**: FR-054 to FR-057 restate rules entry R2 states in more binding detail. Where R3's wording is terser, a reader implementing from this spec alone would build something R2's requirements do not permit — several items below test exactly that.

## The four conventions, against their source

- [x] CHK001 Is the toast auto-dismiss interval quantified? [Clarity, Spec §FR-054] — "auto-dismissing" is unmeasurable as written; R2's corresponding requirement fixes a specific interval. → **Covered**: `contracts/ux-conventions.md` quotes R2's `FR-034` as binding — five seconds from the toast appearing.
- [x] CHK002 Is a manual dismiss control required on each toast? [Gap, Spec §FR-054] — R2 requires the timer never be the only way out of a toast; FR-054 does not restate it. → **Covered**: The same row — "every toast MUST also carry a dismiss control, so the timer is never the only way out of one"; `research.md` E-2 puts a close `Button` on each.
- [x] CHK003 Is the banner's own message specified, as the write-refusal message is? [Gap, Spec §FR-057] — FR-057 quotes "Changes need a connection" for the refusal but leaves the banner's text unstated. → **Covered**: `contracts/ux-conventions.md` — the banner reads "Can't reach the server. Reconnecting.", binding exactly as quoted from R2's `FR-035`.
- [x] CHK004 Is the discriminator between a lost connection and a rejected write stated in this spec? [Gap, Spec §FR-057, §FR-058] — without it, every permission refusal raises the connection banner. The distinction is the requirement, and it lives in R2 rather than here. → **Covered**: `contracts/ux-conventions.md` §`OT-UX-017` and `research.md` E-5 — a transport failure raises the banner, a server refusal raises a toast, and the distinction is stated as the requirement.
- [x] CHK005 Are toast stacking order and any ceiling on simultaneous toasts specified? [Gap, Spec §FR-054] — "stacked" fixes neither which end new toasts enter nor what happens past a screenful. → **Covered**: `contracts/ux-conventions.md` — newest nearest the corner, and R2 deliberately fixes no ceiling.
- [x] CHK006 Is a toast kind assigned to each write outcome this feature produces? [Completeness, Spec §FR-054, §FR-017] — four kinds are fixed; the mapping is not. FR-017's mail failure is the ambiguous one: the write succeeded, so it is neither a plain success nor FR-058's rejected write. → **Covered**: `contracts/ux-conventions.md` *Which kind, where* maps every outcome this feature produces, sending `FR-017`'s mail failure to **warning**.
- [x] CHK007 Is the "info" toast kind's absence of a caller in this entry recorded? [Coverage, Spec §FR-054] — a requirement for a kind nothing raises is untestable here; is that stated deliberately? → **Covered**: The last row of that same table, and `plan.md` *Complexity Tracking* records the callerless `info` kind as a declared decision.
- [x] CHK008 Is "matching the layout they replace" measurable? [Measurability, Spec §FR-055] — R2 states a zero tolerance for shift; verify FR-055's "MUST NOT shift layout" carries the same strength. → **Covered**: `contracts/ux-conventions.md` quotes R2's "the tolerance is zero" and holds it with row heights and column widths shared between skeleton and table.
- [x] CHK009 Are skeleton requirements defined for both panels, or only for the list that has an acceptance scenario? [Coverage, Spec §FR-055] — story 1 scenario 13 covers the Invitations tab; the roster's skeleton has no scenario. → **Covered**: `contracts/ux-conventions.md` and `plan.md`'s structure name two skeleton components, one per panel.
- [x] CHK010 Is FR-056's re-query obligation scoped to distinguish screen data from the shell frame around it? [Clarity, Spec §FR-056] — as written, "a revisited screen MUST re-query" could be read to forbid a persistent frame that R2 requires. → **Covered**: `contracts/ux-conventions.md` §`OT-UX-006` — "The rule's subject is the screen"; a frame persisting across navigation is framework behaviour, not a cache the requirement forbids.
- [x] CHK011 Are requirements defined for what clears the connection banner? [Gap, Spec §FR-057] — the banner's appearance is specified; its removal is not. → **Covered**: The same table — it clears on the next request that does reach the server, and "Reconnecting" obliges no retry cadence.

## Read failures and states

- [x] CHK012 Are requirements defined for a failed *read* on either tab? [Gap, Spec §FR-055, §FR-058] — FR-058 governs rejected writes and FR-055 governs loading; a roster query that fails has neither a state nor a message. → **Resolved**: `FR-055a` — a failed read replaces its panel with an explanatory state offering a retry, never an empty list and never a standing skeleton.
- [x] CHK013 Is an empty state specified for the Accounts roster, or is its non-emptiness stated as an invariant? [Coverage, Spec §FR-023, §FR-036] — FR-023 covers the invitations list only. → **Resolved**: `FR-036` states the invariant rather than inventing a state — the admin reading the roster is on it, and `FR-049` keeps one active account standing at every moment.
- [x] CHK014 Is the expired invitation's marking specified in a form that does not rely on colour alone? [Gap, Spec §FR-022] — "marked expired" fixes no affordance. → **Resolved**: `FR-022` — the marking is carried by text on the row rather than by colour alone.
- [x] CHK015 Are requirements defined for how long the roster and invitations lists remain usable as they grow? [Gap, Spec §FR-018, §FR-036] — neither pagination, virtualization, nor a stated ceiling appears; SC-006 requires an admin answer the roster question "without scrolling to a second screen". → **Covered**: `research.md` A-5 with `plan.md`'s *Performance Goals* and *Scale/Scope* — a team under twenty (`OT-SCOPE-001`) is the stated ceiling, which is why neither list paginates.

## The Invite form

- [x] CHK016 Do FR-005 and FR-008 agree on what the modal may contain? [Conflict, Spec §FR-005, §FR-008] — FR-005 fixes "one email field and a submit control, and nothing else"; FR-008 requires an inline error carrying a control beside it, inside that modal. → **Resolved**: `FR-005` now scopes "nothing else" to what the modal *offers*; a field's own error output, and the remedy control beside it, are not additions to that composition.
- [x] CHK017 Do FR-006 and FR-059 agree on the submit control's enabled state? [Conflict, Spec §FR-006, §FR-059] — FR-006 requires it stay enabled and never go dead; FR-059 requires in-flight state on the control itself. → **Resolved**: `FR-006` now scopes its prohibition to validation state — no invalid field disables the control — and `FR-059`'s in-flight state answers a submission, standing only while the write is outstanding.
- [x] CHK018 Are requirements defined for submission without the field ever losing focus? [Gap, Spec §FR-006] — validation is specified on blur; a user who types and submits directly has bypassed every stated check. → **Covered**: `research.md` D-3 and `contracts/server-mutators.md` — `InviteState` returns `malformed`, `has_account` and `has_invitation` from the submit as well, rendered the same way as the blur answers.
- [x] CHK019 Are the two duplicate checks specified as to when they run relative to the submission? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008, §FR-009, §SC-010] — SC-010 requires the admin be told "before they submit", which constrains the check's timing more tightly than FR-006's "on blur" does. → **Covered**: `research.md` D-3, `contracts/accounts-screen.md`'s blur-answer table and `data-model.md`'s `AddressCheck` put both checks on blur, ahead of submit.
- [x] CHK020 Are requirements defined for dismissing the modal by means other than Cancel and Escape? [Gap, Spec §FR-011] — a click outside the dialog is neither permitted nor forbidden. → **Resolved**: `FR-011` — a press outside the dialog does not close it, so a typed address is discarded only by an explicit act.
- [x] CHK021 Is the inline error's relationship to the field specified for assistive technology? [Gap, Spec §FR-006, §FR-007] — the errors are required to be inline; association with the control they describe is not stated. → **Covered**: `research.md` D-3 — R1's `SignInForm` shape, `validationBehavior="aria"` with `FieldError` bound to the field.

## The in-page jump

- [x] CHK022 Is the transient highlight's duration or dismissal condition specified? [Gap, Spec §FR-008] — "transient" is unquantified, and the plan carries this forward as an open assumption. → **Covered**: `research.md` *Assumptions carried forward* 1 and `contracts/accounts-screen.md` — it clears on a short interval or the next interaction, whichever comes first.
- [x] CHK023 Are focus-management requirements defined for the jump? [Gap, Spec §FR-008] — the sequence closes a modal, changes the selected tab and scrolls; where focus lands determines whether the affordance works at all for a keyboard or screen-reader user. → **Resolved**: `FR-008b` — focus moves to the account's row, so a keyboard reader lands where a sighted one is looking.
- [x] CHK024 Is the tab change required to be announced to assistive technology? [Gap, Spec §FR-008, §FR-003] — a silent tab switch plus a visual highlight conveys the outcome through sight alone. → **Resolved**: `FR-008b` — the jump announces its outcome to assistive technology, naming the account whose row was reached.
- [x] CHK025 Are requirements defined for the case where the target row is already in view, or cannot be brought into view? [Coverage, Spec §FR-008] → **Resolved**: `FR-008b` — bringing the row into view is a no-op where it is already in view, and the focus move, the announcement and the highlight all happen whether or not any scrolling was needed.
- [x] CHK026 Is the highlight required to be perceivable without relying on colour? [Gap, Spec §FR-008] → **Resolved**: `FR-008b` — the transient highlight is carried by more than colour.

## Controls, confirmation and state

- [x] CHK027 Is the text of the last-admin disabled reason specified, or left to implementation? [Gap, Spec §FR-050] — the requirement fixes that a reason appears inline and is not hidden, not what it says. → **Resolved**: `FR-050` fixes the string — "The last active admin can't be deactivated."
- [x] CHK028 Is the disabled control required to remain reachable and announced rather than merely visible? [Coverage, Spec §FR-050] — "disabled with its reason stated inline" and "MUST NOT be hidden" both address sighted reading only. → **Resolved**: `FR-050` — the control stays reachable by keyboard and its reason is associated with it programmatically, so a reader who never sees the text beside it still meets it.
- [x] CHK029 Is reactivation's confirmation content specified, as deactivation's is? [Gap, Spec §FR-044] — FR-044 pins what deactivation's confirmation must name and says nothing about reactivation's. → **Resolved**: `FR-044` now pins both — reactivation's confirmation names what it restores and says no new link or invitation is issued.
- [x] CHK030 Is FR-059's "its own control" defined for a row-level action? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-059] — whether the pressed control, the row, or the table shows the pending state is not stated. → **Covered**: `research.md` C-4 and `contracts/ux-conventions.md` — `useActionState`'s pending flag, per control.
- [x] CHK031 Are requirements defined for the tab's behaviour when a write completes on the tab that is not selected? [Coverage, Spec §FR-003, §FR-056] — the jump can leave a toast raised from the Invitations tab while Accounts is selected. → **Resolved**: `FR-003a` — no write moves the selected tab, and the toast region and connection banner render at page level, so an outcome raised from one tab is seen while the other is selected.
- [x] CHK032 Is keyboard operation of the two tabs specified, or inherited by reference? [Traceability, Spec §FR-003] — FR-003 fixes the tabs and their default selection but names no interaction contract. → **Covered**: `research.md` D-1 and `contracts/accounts-screen.md` — React Aria's `Tabs` supplies the roving tabindex, arrow keys and `aria-controls` that `FR-030`/`OT-UX-018` require.
- [x] CHK033 Are the exact user-facing strings this feature fixes collected anywhere a reviewer can check them against R2's? [Traceability, Spec §FR-023, §FR-057] — two strings are quoted in the spec and at least one more is fixed by R2 and not restated here. → **Covered**: `contracts/ux-conventions.md` is that collection point, quoting R2's strings as binding; `contracts/accounts-screen.md` carries this feature's own.

## Notes
